top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a mature, independently reproduced measurement capability: magic-wavelength optical lattice clocks, where Sr, Yb and Hg clocks in several laboratories agree at the 1e-18 level and already deliver millimetre-scale redshift tests and bounds on constants and dark-matter couplings. Katori (concept and first Sr clock) and Ye (scaling to the present accuracy and stability) give a defensible two-name allocation, and the citation is scoped to the lattice clock itself, distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 has a stronger conceptual story but an incomplete credit chain (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Fu-Kane-Mele 3D work fall outside the trio), so I rank it second, above no award.
recusal_note: No direct collaboration with Katori or Ye; indirect link through PhD advisor Sune Svanberg and a stay in John Hall's lab (broader laser-spectroscopy community). No tie to the B032 candidates.
